text_blocks.snippet: Rubella, also known as German measles, typically clears up on its own within 7 to 10 days. The rash itself usually lasts about three days, but swollen glands can persist for a week or more, and joint pain can linger for a couple of weeks, especially in adults.

list.snippet: Rash: The characteristic rubella rash typically lasts for around three days.
Swollen Glands: Swollen lymph nodes, especially around the head and neck, can persist for a week or more.
Joint Pain: Joint pain, more common in adults, can last for more than two weeks.
Overall Recovery: Most people with rubella recover within a week, but adults may take a little longer.
Contagious Period: Rubella is contagious for about a week before the rash appears and up to a week after the rash disappears.

text_blocks.snippet: If you're concerned about rubella, especially if you're pregnant, consult with a healthcare professional for proper diagnosis and management.

text_blocks.snippet: Rubella, also known as German measles, is a viral infection that typically resolves on its own without specific treatment. However, supportive care measures can help alleviate symptoms and promote recovery.
snippet_highlighted_words: typically resolves on its own without specific treatment

list.snippet: Rest: Get plenty of rest to allow your body to fight the infection.
Hydration: Drink plenty of fluids to prevent dehydration.
Over-the-counter medications: Acetaminophen (Tylenol) or ibuprofen (Advil) can help relieve fever, pain, and discomfort.
Isolation: Avoid contact with others to prevent spreading the virus.

text_blocks.snippet: In rare cases, rubella can lead to complications, such as:
Arthritis, Encephalitis, and Congenital rubella syndrome (if contracted during pregnancy).
If you experience any complications or severe symptoms, seek medical attention immediately.

The best way to prevent rubella is through vaccination with the measles, mumps, and rubella (MMR) vaccine. It is recommended that everyone receive two doses of the vaccine, typically given in childhood.
